translation:
A Dialogue with Lord Jagannath

In writing the parchari (hagiographic account) of Jivanji Maharaj, Shyamdasji Maharaj has drawn our attention to several events. Jivanji Maharaj's coming into the world had a definite purpose — it is well known that he appeared for the welfare of his own devotees (nij-jans). Haridas Nadiyada, too, stated this at the very outset of the satsang gathering. In the course of the gathering he merely mentioned that Jivanji Maharaj had spent a night inside the world-famous temple of Jagannath. But Shyamdasji, in his parchari of Jivandasji, has also described the conversation that took place between Jivanji Maharaj and Lord Jagannath.

_Tum kaho ihaan kahaan te aaye, aras paras mili kanth lagaaye._
_Kehi kaaran tum bhaye prakaashaa, tabahi bole Shri Jeevandaasaa._
("Tell me, from where have you come here?" — saying this, the two embraced each other, neck to neck. "For what reason have you appeared here?" — then Shri Jivandasji spoke in reply.)

At evening time, while having darshan of Jagannathji in the temple, Jivanji Maharaj had entered into bhava-samadhi. Meanwhile, as the hour grew late, the priests closed the temple and departed. Then, at midnight, Lord Jagannath

woke Jivandasji and asked him, "O Saint! From where have you come here?" So saying, the two embraced each other, neck to neck, and He asked the reason for his coming. Jivanji Maharaj replied, "I have received the command of the supremely gracious Ram; therefore I have come for the welfare of His own devotees." Lord Jagannath said, "O supreme saint! The Lord's divine play (kreeda) is infinite — no one can fathom its limit. I too am but one small portion (ansh) of Him, and day and night I sing His praises."

Hearing this, Jivanji Maharaj said, "O Lord! You alone are capable of knowing how much love I bear toward the Supreme Being. But I have a longing (bhaav) to witness Your rasa-leela (the divine circle-dance). Please grant me its darshan." On hearing this, Lord Jagannath performed the rasa-leela that very night, together with all the gopis. Instruments began to play, and with deep devotional feeling He created an atmosphere steeped in loving bhakti.
